root_cause.text: In the macb Ethernet driver’s TX completion path (`macb_tx_unmap()`/`macb_tx_poll()`), TX SKBs were freed with `napi_consume_skb()` even after `tx_ptr_lock` changes caused that code to run with interrupts disabled, violating the API’s context requirements and triggering the softirq warning.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that “after commit 6bc8a5098bf4 … the freeing of TX SKBs is performed with IRQs disabled” and that `napi_consume_skb()` “is not intended to be called in an IRQ disabled context”; the patch changes `napi_consume_skb(tx_skb->skb, budget);` to `dev_consume_skb_any(tx_skb->skb);` in `drivers/net/ethernet/cadence/macb_main.c`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use a context-independent skb free helper in macb_tx_unmap so transmit completion can release packets safely outside NAPI budget handling.
intent_record.what: In macb_tx_unmap(), the call to release tx_skb->skb was changed from napi_consume_skb(tx_skb->skb, budget) to dev_consume_skb_any(tx_skb->skb), while still setting tx_skb->skb to NULL afterward.
intent_record.how: The skb is now freed using a context-agnostic helper instead of the NAPI-specific consume function, which avoids relying on a budget parameter and makes the unmap path safe to call outside NAPI poll context.

grouping_result.intent: Use a context-independent skb free helper in macb_tx_unmap so transmit completion can release packets safely outside NAPI budget handling.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause: TX SKBs were being freed with napi_consume_skb() in a context where interrupts were disabled. Replacing it with a context-independent skb free helper in macb_tx_unmap fixes the unsafe completion path.

candidates.rationale: This is the freeing call used in the TX completion path. According to the root cause, it was unsafe after tx_ptr_lock changes caused the code to run with interrupts disabled, because napi_consume_skb() has context requirements that were violated, triggering the warning.

vuln_statements.explanation: This TX completion free path uses napi_consume_skb() in macb_tx_unmap(), which became unsafe after tx_ptr_lock changes caused the code to execute with interrupts disabled, violating the API context requirements and triggering the softirq warning.

commit 138badbc21a0113ce783270c426210d6451da5d1
Author: Robert Hancock <robert.hancock@calian.com>
Date:   Mon May 9 13:46:35 2022 -0600

    net: macb: use NAPI for TX completion path
    
    This driver was using the TX IRQ handler to perform all TX completion
    tasks. Under heavy TX network load, this can cause significant irqs-off
    latencies (found to be in the hundreds of microseconds using ftrace).
    This can cause other issues, such as overrunning serial UART FIFOs when
    using
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is TX SKB freeing in the TX completion path using the wrong context. In this commit, that logic is already changed: `macb_tx_unmap()` no longer calls `dev_kfree_skb_any(tx_skb->skb);` but instead calls `napi_consume_skb(tx_skb->skb, budget);` in the TX completion path (`macb_tx_complete()`), and the TX path is now explicitly moved into NAPI (`macb_tx_poll`). The snippet also shows the interrupt handler scheduling `napi_tx` instead of directly completing TX, and `macb_tx_complete()` runs under `spin_lock(&queue->tx_ptr_lock)` inside the NAPI poll. This means the specific bug from the root cause is not present in this version and the fix is already applied.
